relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Naboth's inherited vineyard lies dangerously close to the palace.
Ahab offers a better field or silver because royal desire sees location before lineage.
Naboth refuses to turn ancestral inheritance into the king's vegetable garden.
The ruler responds to a lawful no by retreating to bed and refusing food.
Jezebel asks why the king has collapsed into resentment.
Ahab retells the exchange while minimizing the sacred reason for Naboth's refusal.
Jezebel interprets kingship as the power to make refusal disappear.
She writes in Ahab's name and turns his seal into delegated violence.
A public fast disguises the coming seizure as communal holiness.
False witnesses are instructed to merge offense against Divine and king, then demand death.
Local elders and nobles obey the palace letter.
Naboth is elevated publicly only so he can be destroyed publicly.
The scripted accusation is performed, and the community stones an innocent landholder.
The execution is reported upward as completed work.
Jezebel tells Ahab death has removed the legal obstacle.
Ahab goes immediately to possess the land, making himself beneficiary of the murder.
The prophetic word enters the stolen vineyard.
Elijah is sent to find the king standing inside the result of state violence.
Have you murdered and also possessed? The question joins blood and property so they cannot be separated.
Ahab calls accountability his enemy; Elijah names a life sold to evil.
The oracle answers one murder with threatened extermination of a household.
Ahab's dynasty is placed beside earlier houses swept away.
Jezebel's own body is threatened with public desecration.
Dogs and birds again become the imagined agents of dynastic erasure.
The narrator emphasizes Jezebel's incitement, but Ahab's seal, throne, and possession remain his responsibility.
The king's religious conduct is described through conquest-era polemic.
Ahab tears clothing, fasts, and walks softly beneath the judgment.
The word returns to Elijah in response to the king's humility.
Disaster is delayed from Ahab to his son, preserving the dynasty's logic of inherited punishment rather than restoring Naboth's family.

contemplative_note: The vineyard exposes the anatomy of state theft: royal desire, wounded entitlement, forged authority, religious theater, compliant officials, false testimony, execution, and possession. Repentance that does not return the land or repair the family remains unfinished.
